text.text: Contract search inside the platform returns poor results when users type a term in Latin script but the stored document uses Cyrillic, or vice versa; about 1 in 5 searches returns zero hits even though the document exists.

detail.text: Serbia uses both Cyrillic and Latin scripts for the same language, and our clients upload contracts in both. When a user types a search term in Latin script and the stored document uses Cyrillic — or the other way around — our search returns no results even though the document is there. We estimated this affects roughly one in five searches based on a sample we pulled from server logs in January 2024. The root cause is that our full-text search index in PostgreSQL treats the two scripts as completely different character sets. We know transliteration is a solved problem in principle, but we have not implemented it because it is not clear where the right place in the pipeline is — at indexing time, at query time, or both — and there are edge cases where the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions. We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks. We want a solution that is robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones, and that does not slow down search response times noticeably.

about.text: Lex Automatika d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2017 by a small group of lawyers and software engineers who were tired of watching contract review eat up entire working weeks. We built a contract lifecycle management platform — KlozuraPro — that handles drafting, clause-level review, approval routing and electronic signature in one place. Today we serve around sixty mid-size companies across Serbia, with clients in manufacturing, distribution, leasing and professional services. Our team of thirty-four people works out of NTP Novi Sad, which lets us stay close to the research community and hire strong engineering talent from the University of Novi Sad. What makes us different is that KlozuraPro was built specifically for the legal and regulatory environment of the Western Balkans. Our clause library, risk logic and template sets reflect Serbian contract law out of the box, so clients are not adapting a tool built for another market. We do not sell legal advice; we sell time savings and a clear audit trail. Our first big customer was a Novi Sad-based food distributor, Agrotrans Vojvodina d.o.o., which cut its average contract turnaround from eleven days to under two. That case study opened doors across the region and we have been growing steadily since.

products.text: ClauseGuard — automated clause-risk scoring and redlining add-on
SignFlow — electronic signature and approval-routing module
TemplateDesk — industry-specific contract template library for Serbian law
KlozuraAPI — REST API for embedding contract workflows into third-party ERP and CRM systems

tech.text: Python-based NLP pipeline (spaCy, custom fine-tuned transformer models trained on Serbian-language contracts)
PostgreSQL with full-text search for document storage
React frontend with a custom clause annotation editor
Docker and Kubernetes on a private cloud hosted in Serbia
PDF and DOCX parsing via Apache Tika and custom post-processing scripts
Rule-based clause classification combined with a fine-tuned BERT-like model for risk scoring
REST API layer built with FastAPI

plans.text: In 2025 we plan to launch localised versions of KlozuraPro for the Hungarian and Romanian markets and to sign at least ten clients outside Serbia. We are also preparing a Series A fundraising round to double the engineering team and build out a dedicated data and compliance function.

rdCapacity.text: We have two ML engineers and one backend engineer available for collaborative research work, with capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development.

pastCollaborations.text: We ran a six-month applied research project in 2022 with a small NLP research group at a Novi Sad technology institute, focused on building our initial Serbian-language clause classifier; the collaboration produced our current training dataset but no published output.
